items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "nucleus"?

Contains the genetic material (chromosomes made of DNA) that controls the activities of the cell.
Controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell (partially permeable).
Jelly-like fluid where most of the chemical reactions of the cell take place.

items.stem: Daniel places red blood cells in one dish and onion epidermis cells in another, both in distilled water, and observes them after 20 minutes. (a) Describe what you would expect to see happen to each type of cell. (b) Explain these observations. (c) Explain why the two types of cell respond differently. (d) Explain why turgor pressure is important for a non-woody plant.
items.answer: (a) Red blood cells swell and burst (lysis); onion cells become turgid. (b) Water enters by osmosis because the solution has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm. (c) Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall that resists expansion and supports the cell; animal cells have only a membrane. (d) Turgid cells press against each other, supporting stems and leaves so that leaves are held up to the light; loss of turgor causes wilting.
items.markingKey: (a) red blood cells [1]; onion cells [1] [2] (b) water potential comparison [1]; osmosis through partially permeable membrane [1] [2] (c) cell wall in plant cells [1]; not in animal cells [1] [2] (d) support [1]; wilting if lost [1] [2]

items.stem: In a biology lesson in Toronto, students examine prepared slides of an artery and a vein cut in cross-section, and a capillary network in a muscle. items.answer: (a) Walls one cell thick give short diffusion distance; many branches give large surface area; narrow lumen slows blood. items.markingKey: (a) two points [2] (b) [2] (c) [2]

items.stem: Priya collects pond animals on a field trip near Colombo. (a) Construct a dichotomous key to identify these organisms. (b) Explain why the key must use features that do not change during the life of the organism or with the season.

items.markingKey: pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium (all correct [2]; one error [1]) [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "vertebrate"?
options: A plant with roots, stems and fronds that reproduces by spores, not seeds.
A hard external skeleton made of chitin that supports and protects an arthropod.
An animal with a backbone (vertebral column).
An invertebrate with jointed legs, a segmented body and an exoskeleton.
items.answer: An animal with a backbone (vertebral column).
items.markingKey: Vertebrate: an animal with a backbone (vertebral column).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "a leaf with green areas that contain chlorophyll and white areas that do not"?
items.answer: Variegated leaf
items.markingKey: Variegated leaf: a leaf with green areas that contain chlorophyll and white areas that do not.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why the small intestine is very long. (b) Explain why a good blood supply to the villi increases the rate of absorption.
items.answer: (a) A long intestine gives a large surface area and more time for digestion and absorption to be completed. (b) Blood carries absorbed nutrients away quickly, maintaining a steep concentration gradient for diffusion.
items.markingKey: (a) surface area [1]; time [1] [2] (b) carries nutrients away [1]; maintains gradient [1] [2]

items.stem: Which smaller molecules join together to form cellulose?
items.answer: glucose
items.markingKey: Cellulose is made from glucose.

items.stem: A student in Toronto states: "Water moves from a concentrated solution to a dilute solution." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Water moves from a dilute solution (higher water potential) to a concentrated solution (lower water potential).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Water moves from a dilute solution (higher water potential) to a concentrated solution (lower water potential). [1]

items.stem: Put these in the order in which water passes through them on its way through a plant: mesophyll cells, xylem in the stem, air spaces, xylem in the leaf.
items.answer: xylem in the stem → xylem in the leaf → mesophyll cells → air spaces
items.markingKey: xylem in the stem → xylem in the leaf → mesophyll cells → air spaces (all correct [2]; one pair reversed [1]) [2]

items.stem: A student in Bangkok states: "Enzymes are killed at high temperatures." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Enzymes are not alive; they are denatured — the active site changes shape.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Enzymes are not alive; they are denatured — the active site changes shape. [1]

items.answer: (i) transport oxygen (haemoglobin) (ii) transports blood cells, ions, glucose, amino acids, hormones, CO₂, urea and plasma proteins (iii) produce antibodies
items.markingKey: (i) transport oxygen (haemoglobin) [1]; (ii) transports blood cells, ions, glucose, amino acids, hormones, CO₂, urea and plasma proteins [1]; (iii) produce antibodies [1] [3]

items.answer: Plants get energy from light; mineral ions are raw materials for making substances such as proteins and chlorophyll.

items.answer: Translocation moves sugar from sources to sinks in any direction, e.g. up to fruits and buds.

items.answer: (i) cell (ii) tissue (iii) organ (iv) organ system

items.stem: A person was vaccinated on day 0 and given a booster dose of the same vaccine on day 30. After the first dose the antibody concentration peaked at 40 arbitrary units on day 14. After the booster it peaked at 200 units on day 33. (a) Calculate how many times greater the peak was after the booster. (b) Explain the difference between the two responses.
items.answer: (a) 5 times (b) The first dose produced memory cells; on the second exposure these produced antibodies faster and in greater amounts (secondary response).
items.markingKey: (a) 200 ÷ 40 = 5 [1] (b) memory cells made after first dose [1]; faster / larger secondary response [1] [3]

items.answer: Heart muscle is supplied by the coronary arteries.

items.answer: (i) growth (ii) movement

items.stem: Jonas says: "Stomata are mainly on the upper surface so they receive more light." Explain whether Jonas is correct.
items.answer: Most stomata are on the lower surface, which reduces water loss; they are for gas exchange, not light absorption.

items.stem: A fat droplet of radius 1 mm is emulsified by bile into 1000 smaller droplets, each of radius 0.1 mm. (surface area of a sphere = 4πr²) Calculate the total surface area before and after emulsification, and the factor by which it increases.
items.answer: before 12.6 mm²; after 125.7 mm²; increase × 10

items.stem: A student builds a model of a short section of DNA. One strand has the base sequence GTGCCTATA. (a) Write the sequence of the complementary strand. (b) Describe the overall shape of the DNA molecule. (c) Calculate the percentage of bases in this double-stranded section that are guanine or cytosine.
items.answer: (a) CACGGATAT (b) Two strands coiled into a double helix, with bases paired in the middle. (c) 44.4%
items.markingKey: (a) [2] (b) two strands [1]; double helix [1] [2] (c) G + C pairs = 4 of 9 pairs [1]; = 44.4% [1] [2]

items.stem: Mohammed placed cubes of agar containing alkali and phenolphthalein (pink) into dilute hydrochloric acid and timed how long each cube took to become colourless. Results table. Length of side of cube / mm: 5, 10, 15, 20. Time to become colourless / s, trial 1: 54, 100, 357, 600; trial 2: 55, 165, 349, 585; trial 3: 54, 168, 343, 614. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Calculate the mean time to become colourless at 10 mm, ignoring any anomalous result. (c) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: (a) Concentration of acid; volume of acid. (b) 166.5 s (c) A line graph: length of side of cube on the x-axis and mean time to become colourless on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two from: concentration of acid; volume of acid; temperature of the acid; type and concentration of agar [2] (b) (165 + 168) ÷ 2 [1] = 166.5 s [1] [2] (c) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; length of side of cube on x-axis and time to become colourless on y-axis [1] [2]

items.stem: A student in Hanoi examines thin sections of a sunflower stem and root under a microscope after staining with a dye that colours lignin red. (a) Describe where the red-stained tissue would appear in each section. (b) Name the tissue that is stained red and explain why it contains lignin. (c) Compare the structure of xylem vessels and phloem sieve tubes. (d) Suggest why the leaves of a plant would wilt if the xylem in its stem were blocked.
items.answer: (a) Stem: in the inner part of vascular bundles arranged in a ring near the outside. Root: in a star shape in the centre. (b) Xylem: lignin makes the walls strong to support the plant and waterproof. (c) Xylem: dead, hollow, lignified, no end walls. Phloem: living sieve tubes with perforated sieve plates, cytoplasm, no lignin. (d) Water could not reach the leaves to replace water lost in transpiration, so cells lose turgor.
items.markingKey: (a) stem [1]; root [1] [2] (b) xylem [1]; support / waterproof [1] [2] (c) two comparisons [2] (d) no water supply [1]; loss of turgor [1] [2]

items.stem: Ines plans an investigation into the effect of pH on the activity of amylase using starch, measuring the time until iodine no longer turns blue-black. (a) Describe a method for this investigation. (b) State one safety precaution.
items.answer: (a) Use buffer solutions of pH 3, 5, 7, 9, 11; equal volumes of amylase and starch in each; same temperature (water bath); measure the time until iodine no longer turns blue-black; repeat three times. (b) Wear eye protection (hydrogen peroxide / acid and alkali buffers can be irritant).
items.markingKey: (a) range of at least five pH values with buffers [1]; same volumes / concentrations [1]; same temperature [1]; measurement [1]; repeats [1] [5] (b) [1]

items.stem: An electron micrograph shows a white blood cell that makes antibodies. It contains a large nucleus, many mitochondria, a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and many vesicles near the cell membrane. (a) State the function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum. (b) Suggest why there are many vesicles near the cell membrane. (c) Explain why these structures could not be seen with a light microscope.
items.answer: (a) Ribosomes on its surface make proteins, which are transported through the RER. (b) The vesicles carry the proteins made by the cell to the membrane for release (antibody (protein) secretion). (c) They are smaller than the limit of resolution of a light microscope; an electron microscope has a much greater resolution.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] ribosomes / protein synthesis; [1] transport [2] (b) transport [1]; release/secretion of proteins at the membrane [1] [2] (c) too small / resolution [2]

items.stem: In a district near Santiago, there were 1334 cases of cholera in 2018. After a new water treatment plant and sewers were built, there were 308 cases in 2021. Calculate the percentage decrease in cases. Explain why the new water treatment plant reduced the number of cases.
items.answer: 76.9%; treatment kills Vibrio cholerae and sewers stop faeces contaminating drinking water.
items.markingKey: (1334 − 308) ÷ 1334 × 100 [1] = 76.9% [1]; kills bacteria / separates sewage from drinking water [1] [3]

items.stem: In a biology lesson in Riyadh, students examine prepared slides of an artery and a vein cut in cross-section, and a capillary network in a muscle. (a) Describe two differences between the artery and the vein that the students would see. (b) Explain how the structure of capillaries is adapted for exchange. (c) Name the vessels that carry blood to and from the liver. (d) Explain why the elastic fibres in artery walls are important.
items.answer: (a) Artery: thicker, muscular, elastic wall and narrower lumen; vein: thinner wall, wider lumen (may look flattened) and valves. (b) Walls one cell thick give short diffusion distance; many branches give large surface area; narrow lumen slows blood. (c) Hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein (to); hepatic vein (from). (d) They stretch when the ventricles pump blood and recoil between beats, smoothing flow and maintaining pressure.

items.stem: Diego collects leaves from trees in a park on a field trip near Bangkok. Their features are: holly: leaf is a single blade, leaf edge has spines; horse chestnut: leaf is divided into leaflets, leaflets spread out from one point; birch: leaf is a single blade, leaf edge has no spines, leaf edge has no lobes, leaf edge is finely toothed; maple: leaf is a single blade, leaf edge has no spines, leaf edge has rounded or pointed lobes, lobes are pointed; beech: leaf is a single blade, leaf edge has no spines, leaf edge has no lobes, leaf edge is smooth. (a) Construct a dichotomous key to identify these organisms. (b) Explain why the key must use features that do not change during the life of the organism or with the season.
items.answer: (a) 1a leaf is divided into leaflets ... horse chestnut; 1b leaf is a single blade ... go to 2 | 2a leaf edge has spines ... holly; 2b leaf edge has no spines ... go to 3 | 3a leaf edge has rounded or pointed lobes ... maple; 3b leaf edge has no lobes ... go to 4 | 4a leaf edge is finely toothed ... birch; 4b leaf edge is smooth ... beech (b) Otherwise the same species could be identified differently at different times (e.g. juveniles or seasonal changes).
items.markingKey: (a) paired contrasting statements at each step [1]; each organism reached at a separate end-point [1]; uses features given, not size or colour [1]; 4 steps [1] [4] (b) features must be constant [1]; reliable identification [1] [2]

items.stem: Mei placed a piece of pondweed in a beaker of dilute sodium hydrogencarbonate solution and counted the bubbles of gas released in one minute with a lamp at different distances. Results table. Distance of lamp from pondweed / cm: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Number of bubbles per minute / bubbles/min, trial 1: 53, 49, 36, 30, 24, 19; trial 2: 53, 44, 36, 31, 24, 18; trial 3: 53, 27, 37, 31, 22, 18. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation.
items.answer: (a) Independent: distance of lamp from pondweed; dependent: number of bubbles per minute. (b) Temperature of the water; concentration of sodium hydrogencarbonate (CO₂).
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = distance of lamp from pondweed [1]; dependent variable = number of bubbles per minute [1] [2] (b) Any two from: temperature of the water; concentration of sodium hydrogencarbonate (CO₂); same piece / mass of pondweed; time allowed to adjust before counting; type of lamp / no other light [2]

items.stem: Isla burned samples of different nuts, each of mass 1.0 g, under a boiling tube containing 20 cm³ of water and recorded the temperature rise. Results table. Type of nut: almond, peanut, hazelnut, walnut. Temperature rise / °C, trial 1: 23.5, 24.7, 26.8, 27.1; trial 2: 23.3, 24.5, 26.3, 28; trial 3: 13.4, 24.6, 25.7, 27.5. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) Explain the results. (c) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) Independent: type of nut; dependent: temperature rise. (b) A larger temperature rise means more energy was transferred to the water, so that nut contains more energy per gram (more fat). (c) Insulate the boiling tube / use a calorimeter to reduce heat loss.
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = type of nut [1]; dependent variable = temperature rise [1] [2] (b) more temperature rise = more energy [1]; linked to fat content [1] [2] (c) Any one from: insulate the boiling tube / use a calorimeter to reduce heat loss; relight the nut until it burns completely; stir the water before reading the thermometer; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the type of nut (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Tomás found that 0.8 cm³ of a 0.5 mg/cm³ vitamin C solution was needed to decolourise 1 cm³ of DCPIP. To decolourise 1 cm³ of DCPIP, 1 cm³ of kiwi fruit juice and 1.5 cm³ of apple juice were needed. (a) Calculate the concentration of vitamin C in each juice. (b) State which juice contains more vitamin C. (c) State two variables that must be controlled to make the comparison fair.
items.answer: (a) kiwi fruit juice: 0.400 mg/cm³; apple juice: 0.267 mg/cm³ (b) kiwi fruit juice (c) volume and concentration of DCPIP; temperature / age of juice / mixing method.
items.markingKey: (a) mass of vitamin C to decolourise = 0.4 mg [1]; 0.4 ÷ 1 = 0.400 [1]; ÷ 1.5 = 0.267 mg/cm³ [1] (b) kiwi fruit juice (smaller volume needed) [1] (c) any two valid [2] [6]

items.stem: Carrot discs were kept in a solution of potassium chloride at 10 °C. In one beaker cyanide (which stops aerobic respiration) was added. The uptake of potassium ions in 2 hours was 61 units without cyanide and 18 units with cyanide. (a) Calculate the percentage decrease in uptake caused by cyanide. (b) Predict the effect of raising the temperature to 5 °C below the optimum for respiration enzymes, and explain. (c) Explain why the investigation used several carrot discs of the same size in each beaker.
items.answer: (a) 70.5% (b) Uptake increases because enzymes in respiration work faster, releasing energy more quickly for active transport. (c) Same surface area for uptake so comparison is fair; several discs reduce the effect of variation between discs.
items.markingKey: (a) (61 − 18) ÷ 61 × 100 [1] = 70.5% [1] [2] (b) increase [1]; faster respiration / more energy [1] [2] (c) same surface area / fair test [1]; reliability [1] [2]

items.stem: Sofia measured the mass lost by potted plants (with the soil surface sealed in plastic) over 24 hours at different temperatures. Results table. Temperature / °C: 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. Mass lost / g, trial 1: 16.7, 28.2, 42, 62.5, 80.5; trial 2: 17.6, 17.3, 44.5, 62, 79.2; trial 3: 17.5, 29.3, 44.4, 61.3, 79.8. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Identify the anomalous result in the table and state what should be done with it. (c) Suggest one way to improve this investigation. (d) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: (a) Humidity; light intensity. (b) Trial 2 at 20 °C (17.3 g); it should be ignored when calculating the mean (or repeated). (c) Use plants of the same species and size. (d) A line graph: temperature on the x-axis and mean mass lost on the y-axis.

items.answer: (a) virus; droplets in the air (b) Vaccination (MMR); each breaks the chain of transmission.

items.stem: On a field trip in Manila, Arjun finds two animals. Animal P has a body temperature that varies with the surroundings and dry, scaly skin. Animal Q has moist skin with no scales and adults with lungs living on land. (a) Name the group to which each animal belongs. (b) Explain why classifying organisms into groups is useful to scientists. (c) Suggest why a scientist might check the classification of animal Q by comparing DNA as well as visible features.
items.answer: (a) P: reptiles; Q: amphibians (b) It shows how organisms are related (common ancestry), makes identification easier and allows predictions about features of newly found organisms. (c) Visible features may be similar because of similar environments (not relationship); DNA base sequences show how closely related organisms are more accurately.
items.markingKey: (a) P reptiles [1]; Q amphibians [1] [2] (b) relationships / evolution [1]; identification or prediction [1] [2] (c) features can mislead (convergence) [1]; DNA similarity = relatedness [1] [2]

items.stem: Nadia destarches a potted plant, then leaves a leaf enclosed in a flask containing soda lime (absorbs CO₂) in light for 6 hours before testing it for starch. Result: the leaf stays orange-brown. (a) Explain why the plant was destarched first. (b) Describe how the plant was destarched. (c) State the conclusion of this investigation. (d) State why ethanol must be heated in a water bath, not with a flame. (e) Write the balanced equation for photosynthesis.
items.answer: (a) To remove starch already present, so any starch found was made during the experiment. (b) It was kept in the dark for about 48 hours. (c) Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis. (d) Ethanol is flammable. (e) 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
items.markingKey: (a) removes starch [1]; fair test / starch must come from photosynthesis in experiment [1] [2] (b) [1] (c) [1] (d) [1] (e) formulae [1]; balancing [1] [2]
